CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION, July 23, 1925.

DEAR SIR, - I am directed to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 14th instant on the above subject, and to state
that you will be further advised on the points you raise at an early date.

Yours very truly,
W. FORAN, Secretary.

The Auditor General.

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, October 12, 1925.

SIR, - On October 4th, 1924, and July 14th, 1925, I wrote you asking the opinion of the Commission as to whether an
inspector of construction employed at a daily rate of $6 or $7 could be paid up to $180 to $210 per month or whether
the amount payable in any one month was limited by the established monthly rate.

On July 23rd, 1925, you replied, stating that further information would be given at an early date.

I have received no further communication from you since and would be pleased if you would send, me the information
as soon as convenient.

Your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Secretary, Civil Service Commission.

NOTE BY A.G. - No reply has been received to date, Dec. 31, 1925.

CORRESPONDENCE - CORRESPONDANCE

Payments to Salaried Physician for Special Medical Services

(Continuation of correspondence on page 1 - 194, Report for 1923 - 24)

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, December 13, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - With reference to request in your letter of the 2nd instant for a reply to a letter you wrote this
Department on May 3, 1924, regarding payments to Dr. W.H. Woods, of Mount. Brydges, I beg to say that on July 1,
1919, a new arrangement was made regarding the remuneration paid by this Department to Dr. Woods; it was decided
to pay him salary at the rate of $1,700 per annum and in addition to give him an allowance of from $100 to $300 per
annum, on account of epidemics.

This arrangement was the result of the Department's effort to curtail expenditures on account of epidemics and it was in
effect before classification became effective. Recently, we made a new arrangement with Dr. Woods, with the approval
of the Civil Service Commission, and we are now paying him salary at a higher rate, but giving him no allowance for
work during epidemics.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.

Allowance to Commissioner W.M. Graham for use of Automobile

(Continuation of correspondence on page 1 - 200, Report for 1923 - 24)

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, December 19, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - In reply to your letter on November 19th, regarding an allowance of $60 a mouth paid to Mr. W.M.
Graham, Indian Commissioner at Regina, Sask., for the use of his automobile, I have to say that this allowance has
been continued for some time, as an examination, of our accounts will show. The allowance has been paid from the
spring of 1918 by ministerial authority, and is intended to identify Mr. Graham for the use of his car on official
business. From October 9, 1923, to February 29, 1924, he was, as you state, paid on a basis of tripe actually made by
him, but as this method was inconvenient, and did not appear to promise any saving, the former arrangement was
resumed.

Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.

The Assistant Auditor General.

Regina Warehouse Account: Amounts due by Employees and others for Goods Purchased

(Continuation of correspondence on page 1 - 214, Report for 1923 - 24)


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, February 10, 1925.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the 27th June, particularly the closing paragraph thereof, I beg to say that your
requirements as therein set forth were brought to the attention of Mr. W.M. Graham, Indian Commissioner,

<!-- page 398 -->
Regina, and he has forwarded a duplicate statement, which I enclose, of the Regina warehouse accounts as at the 31st,
March, 1924, and the 31st December, 1924. Mr. Graham has drawn attention to information in the remark column to
the effect that several of the accounts have since been paid and adjusted.

Your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEan, Asst. Deputy and Sec'y.

The Auditor General.

AUDITOR GENERALS OFFICE, February 11, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the, 10th inst., enclosing a copy of a statement, received from,
Mr. Graham, of the Warehouse Accounts at Regina, with adjustments.

In this statement I notice amounts remaining unpaid by members of Mr. Graham's staff, as follows: -

E.S. Biggs, $16, $10.30 of which was incurred prior to April 1, 1924.

M. Christianson, $10.

W.J. Hay, $14.40, incurred prior to April 1, 1924.

E.O. Smitton, $24.15.

I think that it might be advisable to inform Mr. Graham that these amount, should he settled before the close of the
current fiscal year.

I notice also that, accounts amounting in all to, $5,734.15, have been written off, the majority of such accounts being
against Indian Agencies, or Indian Schools. I understand that Mr. Graham has discretionary powers with regard to the
issue of those stores to the Indians and Indian institutions and that he can determine what articles may be issued to the
Indians free of charge and what on repayment. Articles issued to others than Indians however, should be issued on
repayment only. In this connection I should like to, be assured that all the charges written off were for goods
distributed free of charge to Indian, or held for such distribution and that none are for goods issued free of cost to
employees or others. I should like special explanations of the following items which have been written off: -

 R.E. Osborne $88 70
 J.B. Templeton 12 00
 V.C. Wilson 31 95
 Dr. Lane       50 00
 Rev. Westgate 60 77
Your obedient servant,
GEORGES GONTHIER, A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General, Indian Affairs.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, March 12, 1925.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the, llth instant relating to Indian warehouse accounts at Regina, I beg to say that Mr.
Indian Commissioner Graham was made aware of your requirements as therein set forth, and he has made the
following report, -

"All the charges, written off the warehouse books were for goods distributed free of charge to Indians or held for such,
distribution, and none are for goods issued free of cost to employees or others."

<!-- page 399 -->

<!-- page 400 -->
"In regard to the items about which special explanation is asked, I have to state that in the case of the item of $88.70
opposite the name of R.E., Osborn, this was originally charged in the books in error against his account personally, but
the items which the charge in question covered were for re-sale to Indians, and to adjust Mr. Osborn's account the item
was written off in like manner as a number of accounts were written off at other Agencies for articles sent for
distribution among Indians."

"The item of $50 opposite the name of Dr. Lane represents a refund on account of dental chair sold to him; the original
price of which was $200. After delivery of the chair to Dr. Lane, however, it was discovered that the seat was lacking,
and $150 was accepted from him in full payment and lose balance written off."

"The item of $60.77 opposite the name of Rev. T.B. Westgate, represents articles shipped for use at the Elkhorn
School, which he undertook to pay as an officer of the Missionary Society. It should have been charged against the
Elkborn School and was written off as a free, issue after it, had been decided to treat in the same way other accounts at
other schools."

"Mr. J.B. Templeton and Mr. V.C. Wilson were at one time clerks at the Qu'Appelle, and Broadview Agencies,
respectively, and when their services were dispensed with it was found that the amounts set opposite their names were
owing by them for goods supplied from the warehouse, but as at that time and subsequently it was found impossible to
make collection the respective items were written off."

Mr. Graham concluded his report by stating that collection of the outstanding accounts named by you will be made
before the close of the current fiscal year.

I may add it is hoped that you will find the foregoing information satisfactory.

Your obedient servant,
J.D. MCLEAN, Act. D.S.G.

The Auditor General.

Note by A.G. - Outstanding account practically all collected.

Indian Trust Fund, Revenue: Asking for List of Leases

(Previous correspondence on page 1 - 221, Report for 1923 - 24)

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 9, 1925.

SIR, - I beg to draw your attention to my letter of April 9th, 1924, in which I requested to be furnished with a list, of
all leases of Indian lands in force on April 1st, 1923, together with full particulars regarding the same, no reply to
which has as yet been received.

In order to be in a position to examine, in a satisfactory manner, this part of the revenue of your department, I should
be supplied, at regular intervals, with full particulars of all leases both as regards the terms, of each lease and the
payments that have been received on account thereof. I have accordingly now to request that you furnish me with a list
of all leases in force on April
